questions.question: Which issues in Project Atlas are blocked, and why?
questions.expected_answer: Four Atlas issues are currently blocked: the refunds API integration (Priya Raman) and the chargeback webhook receiver (Diego Santos) are blocked directly on the payment provider - the v3 refunds sandbox has not been delivered and the v3 webhook signing spec has not been published. The refund reconciliation nightly job and the support-agent refund request API (both Aisha Okonkwo) are blocked transitively on the refunds integration. A fifth, the Beacon usage event schema alignment, was blocked on Beacon's v2 envelope freeze and is now resolved.
expected_sources: Integrate refunds API with the payment provider sandbox
Refund request API for support agents

questions.question: What was the original due date of the Atlas issue "Integrate refunds API with the payment provider sandbox", and how many times did it move?
questions.expected_answer: The refunds API integration was originally due 2026-06-15. It moved twice, to 2026-07-10 and then to 2026-08-07, both times because the payment provider had not delivered the v3 refunds sandbox.
expected_sources: Integrate refunds API with the payment provider sandbox
questions.note: Names the issue explicitly. Atlas has four refunds issues with different histories, so a question phrased as "the refunds work" is ambiguous and would fail the eval against a correct answer about a different issue.

questions.question: Why did the Atlas billing launch move from June to August?
questions.expected_answer: The launch moved from 2026-06-30 to 2026-08-14 because the refunds epic was blocked on the payment provider's v3 refunds sandbox, and the launch readiness review was a no-go on the grounds that a biller which cannot process a refund is not launchable.
expected_sources: Launch readiness review for the billing platform
Integrate refunds API with the payment provider sandbox

questions.question: Which Atlas work was held up by another team rather than by a vendor?
questions.expected_answer: The usage event schema alignment was held up by Beacon, which could not freeze the v2 event envelope until the identity resolution rewrite landed. It was blocked for about four weeks and resolved on 2026-07-03.
expected_sources: Usage event schema alignment with Beacon

questions.question: Who owns the chargeback work and what is the security concern raised on it?
questions.expected_answer: Diego Santos owns the chargeback webhook receiver. Julian Vega objected to shipping it without signature verification, because an unauthenticated webhook that opens dispute records is an abuse vector even behind a feature flag. It remains blocked rather than shipped unverified.
